chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: His sisters' schooling and meeting Cachao
summary: His sisters attended a school run by black nuns, and he describes meeting young Cachao and the musical Lopez family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. Okay. At that time your family is increasing, you - What were the other children now....
There was Estela, there was Graciel, there was Rogelio, Jr. and Martha.
Okay. Did any of them get the music influence . . .
Okay. What were they doing at that time when they were -------
At that time they went to - they was in school - they were younger than me, they was going to Hermanas Oblatas. That was an organization from New Orleans, black
nuns, that they opened that particular private school in Havana, Catholic school, by black nuns.
Okay, so Graciela and Estela went to the...
And what were they, singing or learning an instrument? Or what?

Not particularly, but my house was so musical that Estela was a singer and Graciela was a singer; my sister Anisa too could sing, so when we moved to Pobolote - before we moved to Pobolote - we moved to Liyano, is another neighborhood, and we - my my son godmother "La Ninita", they had a sexteto that's where I met Cachao, he was a little kid about ......

The bass player, his father was a fantastic bass player from the Sinfonica, his brother Macho, they dalled him Macho, and a piano player too. The whole family were musicians. The mother was flute player and another sister was pianist and it was a musical family.
